title: Every outside program is optional: one seam per capability, and a setup that lacks one runs without it
description:
orbital reads two outside programs, git and a pager, and is about to be
public. The README promises "git, and nothing else" and `docs/design.md`
calls the pager "a convenience, not a dependency". The code keeps neither
promise yet. Measured 2026-09-02 at 58e1f79:

- The pager is reached by name from `render::page` (`pager::open`) and wired
  by name in `cli::wire` (`Pager::new(RealRunner, ..)`). A machine with no
  pager gets a warning about the pager on every run, on every invocation.
- git is reached by name from `read::log`, and its argv is known to three
  modules rather than one, so a change to how orbital calls it is a change in
  three places and a test in none of them.
- The editor is reached only from `note::edit`, which is the shape the other
  two want.

## What this is not

Not a plugin system, and not configuration. Nothing here lets a setup
substitute a different pager or a different git; the seam exists so that a
setup which lacks one runs without it, and so that the argv lives in one
place. A setup that wants a different pager already has `PAGER`.

## The seam

One trait per capability, named for what the capability provides rather than
for the program that provides it:

| capability | trait | today |
|---|---|---|
| the change log | `Changes` | `read::log`, git by name |
| paging output | `Paging` | `render::page`, pager by name |
| editing a note | `Editing` | `note::edit`, editor by name |

Each has exactly one implementation in this crate and each implementation
names its program once. `cli::wire` chooses the implementation; nothing below
`cli/` knows a program name.

## Absence is a state, not a failure

The distinction the current code loses. A setup with no pager is not a setup
whose pager failed: the first is ordinary and the second is worth saying
something about. So each capability resolves to one of three things at wire
time — present, absent, or present and broken — and only the third is drawn
on screen.

That is also what makes the warning stop. Today the warning fires on absence,
which is the common case on a machine that never had a pager, so the reader
learns to ignore a line that would matter if it ever said something else.

## Done when

- Each outside program sits behind one seam, and a setup that lacks one runs
  without it rather than warning about it on every frame.
- The argv for each is spelled in one place, and a test asserts the whole
  argv rather than the subcommand.
- Nothing under `read/`, `render/` or `note/` names a program.
- A setup whose pager cannot be executed is told so, naming the pager, and
  a setup that has no pager is told nothing.

## Not in this bead

- Choosing a pager, or reading `PAGER`. That is `orb-0tp.4`.
- The editor seam's own tests, which want a fake that can fail mid-write and
  are a bead of their own.
- Anything about git's own configuration. orbital reads a repository; it does
  not manage one.

## Why now

The promise in the README is the reason this is P1 rather than P3. A public
repository whose README describes a dependency model the code does not have
is a bug report waiting to be filed by somebody who tried it, and the fix
after that report is the same fix as this one plus an apology.

title: A pager or an editor that cannot be run is reported as git's failure
description:
`read::run::RunFailure::from_exit` classifies the stderr and exit of every
subprocess orbital runs, and the screen phrases the result as git's. A pager
or an editor that cannot be run (`Exec`) reaches the same mapping, so a
missing pager or a typo in `pager_command` is drawn as "git could not be
run". The reader is sent to check git when git was never reached.

## Done when

- A failure to run a pager or an editor is reported on screen as that
  program's, naming which one, and a git failure as git's.
- Tested with a runner whose pager cannot be executed, asserting the words
  the screen shows.

title: group/mod.rs's tests are one module every grouping change appends to
description:
`group/mod.rs`'s tests are one module every grouping change appends to, and it
is now long enough that a reader looking for the ordering rules reads the
whole file to find out there are none. 1,340 lines, 61 tests, one `mod
tests`.

Split it by what each test is about, and let the module names say it. On a
first pass the tests fall into four groups:

- ordering within a type
- ordering between types
- what an untyped entry does
- what an empty group does

## Not a behaviour change

No test is deleted and none is rewritten. A test that moves keeps its name,
its body and its assertions; only the module around it is new. The check is
that the count is the same before and after and that `cargo test group::`
runs the same number.

## Done when

- `group/mod.rs`'s tests are split into named modules by subject.
- The test count is unchanged.
- No test body changed.

title: phrase.rs is one file every screen change edits
description:
`phrase.rs` is one file every screen change edits, so two seats working on
different screens collide in it for no reason other than where the words
live. Measured over the last forty commits: eleven touch `phrase.rs`, and
nine of those eleven touch exactly one other file.

Move each phrase next to the screen that says it, and leave `phrase.rs`
holding only the ones more than one screen shares.

## What stays

A phrase used by two or more screens stays, because moving it to one of them
makes the other import from a screen it has nothing else to do with. On
today's count that is six phrases, all of them about failure: the four
tracker states, "nothing to show", and the truncation marker.

## What moves

Everything else, which is thirty-one phrases across five screens. Each goes
into the module that draws it, private, with the test that asserts its
wording moving with it.

## Not a wording change

No phrase changes. A diff that shows a word changing is a diff that has done
something this bead did not ask for, and the check for that is that the
strings are identical before and after — `git diff -w --stat` should show
the same total additions and deletions.

## Done when

- `phrase.rs` holds only phrases more than one screen uses.
- Every moved phrase is private to the module that draws it.
- No phrase's wording changed.

title: Change sources sit behind one seam outside cli/, and a local repository is one implementation of it
description:
Change sources sit behind one seam outside `cli/`, and a local repository is
one implementation of it rather than the only shape the code knows.

Today `cli::wire` opens the repository itself and hands a path down, so a
source that is not a path on this machine cannot be added without changing
every layer it passes through. The path reaches `read::log`, `read::refs`
and `group::order`, and each of the three does its own thing with it.

## The shape

One trait, `Changes`, with the three questions the rest of the crate asks:

```rust
trait Changes {
    fn entries(&self, since: Option<&Rev>) -> Result<Vec<Entry>>;
    fn refs(&self) -> Result<Vec<Ref>>;
    fn head(&self) -> Result<Rev>;
}
```

`LocalRepository` implements it and is the only implementation this crate
ships. The point is not to have two; the point is that the layers below
`cli/` name the trait, so the second one costs a file rather than a
refactor.

## Why the boundary is at cli/

Because that is where the process's own facts already live — the working
directory, the environment, the argv. A layer that has to be told where the
repository is has not been given a dependency; it has been given a
responsibility it cannot discharge, and every test of it has to construct a
repository on disk to say anything at all.

## Done when

- One trait names what a change source provides, and the local repository
  implements it.
- `cli/` names the trait and not the implementation.
- `read/` and `group/` take the trait, and their tests take a fake rather
  than a temporary directory.
- No path to a repository is passed below `cli/`.

## Blocked on

`orb-0tp.2`, which pulls the argv into one place — this seam wants that done
first or it moves the same argv twice. And `orb-rer.9`, which is the last
caller in `render/` still reaching for a path.
